solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S020-01.notes: Colon clause defines the blank: readable as acceptance or refusal = equivocal. Context makes it solvable, but 'equivocal' is a vocabulary word many test-takers don't know; B/C/D don't fit.

flags: minor: in the real stilt experiment (Wittlinger et al. 2006) the legs were changed at the food source, which matches the passage; fine as written
S020-02.notes: If ants count steps, longer strides overshoot and shorter strides fall short. A would weaken; B and D are irrelevant.

S020-03.notes: Sampling-bias objection: gym members aren't representative of residents. A doesn't undercut the claim; B slightly strengthens it; C is off topic.

S020-04.notes: Singular subject 'archive' takes 'is'; the plural nouns in the relative clause are the trap. C/D leave no finite verb.

S020-05.notes: Two independent clauses, and the second explains the first, so a colon fits. B is a comma splice and C a run-on; D, a semicolon followed by 'and', is wrong.

flags: minor: 'Nevertheless' (despite this) is a slightly loose contrast for an exception to a general pattern; 'However' would be more precise, but no other choice competes
S020-06.notes: Contrast between most bats hunting at night and a few species flying by day. Therefore, For instance and Likewise don't signal contrast.

S020-07.notes: Only D states a similarity (both published first novels at 60 or older). The facts check out: Fitzgerald's first novel came in 1977 when she was 60, Offshore won the Booker in 1979, and Wilder published in 1932 at about 65.

S020-08.notes: Established date of about 500 BCE, then conflicting radiocarbon dates near 800 BCE, then an explanation (the pottery style stayed in use longer). D reverses the roles of the pottery and the new date; A and C are not in the text.

S020-09.notes: Text 2 says the decline started around 1310 because trade moved downriver, and the plague then sharply reduced an already shrinking population. A and C overstate the position; D contradicts Text 2's use of the tax records.

S020-10.notes: Winter rose 300/1000 = 30% and summer 400/4000 = 10%, so A is accurate and supports the claim. B is the absolute-count trap and argues the opposite; C and D don't address percentage change.
